ideas.name: Same Half-Hour Stock Return Continuation
ideas.claim: A stock’s return in a half-hour interval tends to continue in the same interval on subsequent trading days.
ideas.quote: However, we find significant continuation of returns at intervals that are multiples of a day and this effect lasts for at least 40 trading days.
ideas.claimed_result: For S&P 500 stocks, the previous-day signal produced an average decile spread of 9.42 basis points in the closing interval and 0.98 basis points in the intraday period; the study period was 2001–2005.
required_data: Intraday prices for individual US stocks

ideas.name: Cross-Sectional End-of-Day Reversal
ideas.claim: Stocks with lower returns from the previous close to one hour before the current close tend to outperform stocks with higher returns during the final half-hour.
ideas.quote: In this paper, we document a novel intraday return predictability: an individual stock return during the early parts of a trading day negatively predicts its return in the cross-section during the last half an hour of a trading day.

rules.market: US individual stocks, including large-cap stocks
rules.timeframe: Final 30 minutes of the trading day
rules.entry: Long lower-return stocks and short higher-return stocks at the start of the final half-hour
rules.filters: Rank stocks by return from the previous close to one hour before the current close; skip the intervening 30 minutes

ideas.claimed_result: The paper reports average long-short returns of 3.55–6.15 basis points per day since 1993, depending on weighting and price filter.
required_data: Intraday prices for individual US stocks
